newsitem.title: MEXICO: TMM says Q4 profits $19.2 mln.
newsitem.headline: TMM says Q4 profits $19.2 mln.

text.p: Mexican transport company Transportacion Maritima Mexicana (TMM) reported 1996 fourth quarter net profits of $19.2 million, 3.1 percent lower than the same period in 1995, the company said on Monday.
The company said earnings per share for the quarter were $0.34 versus $0.35 in the same quarter the previous year.
Net income for the quarter was $185.1 million, 5.8 percent below the quarter in 1995. TMM attributed the income drop to the sale of Global Reefer Carriers (GRC) in June 1996.
Gross profits were $19.7 million, or 42.7 percent lower than the previous year. Operating earnings were $540,000 against $16.3 million in the last three months of 1995.
TMM also presented adjusted results to allow for a comparison from before the GRC sale. With the adjustment, the quarter's net sales was $184.6 million, up 18.85 percent from period in 1995.

"The increase was due to greater volume transported in the line division, greater tankers, suppliers and ship rentals, in addition to increased income from railroad, autotransport and port businesses," TMM said.
Net profits excluding the GRC sale were $98.2 million, down 10.5 percent from $109.7 million in the last quarter of 1995.
